title: Expression of CGRP in the Trigeminal Ganglion and Its Effect on the Polarization of Macrophages in Rats with Temporomand

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract / Results (CD86 macrophage surge in TG)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract states: 'within 24 h of inducing temporomandibular arthritis using CFA, there was a significant surge in CD86 positive macrophages within the ganglion.' However, the Results section reports the actual statistic for day 1 as p = 0.7376 ('These macrophages increased progressively on days 1, 3, and 7 compared to the control group... p = 0.7376, p = 0.1193, p < 0.0001, and p < 0.0001, respectively'), which is far from statistically significant. The abstract's claim of a 'significant surge' at 24h directly contradicts the non-significant p-value reported for day 1 in the body text.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, pain behavior section (HWT comparison to control)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states 'The HWT was notably reduced on days 1, 3, 7, and 14 post-injection when compared to controls (p = 0.2747, p = 0.0102, p = 0.0017, and p = 0.3946, respectively).' The p-values for day 1 (0.2747) and day 14 (0.3946) are not statistically significant, contradicting the claim that HWT was 'notably reduced' at all four time points.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, pain behavior section (CGRP effect on HWT)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states 'CGRP injections without the antagonist led to decreased HWT at these same time points compared to the saline group (p = 0.0024, p = 0.3595, p = 0.0436, respectively).' The middle p-value (0.3595, day 3) is not statistically significant, yet the sentence implies a consistent decreasing effect across all three time points without qualification.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, Fig. 3B (CD86-positive M1 macrophages in TG)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text claims macrophages 'increased progressively on days 1, 3, and 7 compared to the control group... (p = 0.7376, p = 0.1193, p < 0.0001, and p < 0.0001, respectively).' The p-values for days 1 and 3 (0.7376 and 0.1193) are non-significant, contradicting the description of a progressive, implied significant increase starting at day 1. This is treated inconsistently compared to the CD206 (M2) data in the same figure, where the authors explicitly note significance was found 'only on day 3... but not on other days,' showing the paper itself distinguishes significant vs non-significant findings elsewhere but fails to do so here.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, Fig. 4B–D (CGRP/CGRP 8-37 effect on TG macrophage polarization)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: 'After the TG was injected with CGRP 8-37 and CGRP, CD86-positive macrophages were significantly increased and decreased, respectively (p < 0.001 and p = 0.1939, respectively).' The second value (p = 0.1939, corresponding to the CGRP-induced decrease in CD86) is not statistically significant, so describing it as 'significantly... decreased' misrepresents the data.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, Fig. 5B (CD86-positive M1 macrophages in TMJ tissue)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: 'CD86-positive M1 macrophages significantly increased one day after CFA treatment, peaking at day 7 (Fig. 5B). These macrophages in the TMJ's surrounding soft tissues surged initially... (p = 0.6672, p = 0.1276, p < 0.0001, p = 0.0033, respectively).' The day 1 p-value (0.6672) is clearly non-significant, directly contradicting the claim of a significant increase 'one day after CFA treatment.'

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, Fig. 5C (CD206-positive M2 macrophages in TMJ tissue)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states CD206-positive macrophages' 'numbers rose progressively on days 1, 3, 7, and 14 (p = 0.0999, p = 0.0008, p = 0.0003, p < 0.0001, respectively).' The day 1 p-value (0.0999) does not meet the conventional significance threshold (p < 0.05), so describing a uniformly significant progressive rise beginning at day 1 is not fully supported by the reported statistics.

The antibody is listed as 'CGRP (CST, ab81887, 1:1000).' The catalog prefix 'ab' is the standard product numbering convention used by Abcam, not Cell Signaling Technology (CST), which uses purely numeric catalog numbers (as correctly shown for CD206: 'CST, 24595'). This indicates a vendor/catalog mismatch — ab81887 is an Abcam product, not a CST product as stated.

The CFA/saline TMJ injection is described as 'bilateral' ('We then administered a bilateral slow injection of 50 µL of either saline or CFA... into the upper compartment of the TMJ'), implying both TMJs were treated identically. However, the subsequent intra-ganglionic (IG) drug delivery procedure is described as targeting 'the ipsilateral trigeminal ganglion,' implying a unilateral, side-specific intervention. The paper does not reconcile how a unilateral IG injection targeting one 'ipsilateral' side relates meaningfully to a bilateral TMJ arthritis model, creating an internal inconsistency in the experimental design description.
